findings.text: non-blocking: the first case asserts only the prefix "still has a live worker", which _live_worker_refusal also produces for the existing launch refusal, so the text alone cannot show which guard answered; the clause unique to this refusal (dispatch.py:508, "cutting its worktree again") is not asserted, though the unchanged-tree and spy assertions still redden under the declared mutation.

non-blocking: the bare `except CrewError` also swallows read_pointer's "live pointer ... is not valid JSON" and "does not hold an object" refusals, so a corrupt pointer for a run whose worker is live silently disables the guard and lets the tree be rebuilt — the defect this node repairs; only the "no live run" case needs to proceed.

non-blocking: the guard passes the raw pointer to _launch_refused_by, which on a placed record carrying a pointer pid and no readable canonical worker record answers refuse (reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1965), so a non-local re-dispatch of a placed run whose worker has ended is refused with the placed-unknown text; that is the shared predicate the plan's next section is dispatched to fix, and this node makes it reachable one step earlier.
